papers.title: SIK3 links synaptic strength to sleep pressure through RhoA signaling
papers.summary: The study shows that SIK3 is required for dendritic spine enlargement induced by chemical LTP in cortical pyramidal neurons and positively regulates spine size in the prefrontal cortex in vivo. It identifies two clashing SIK3-RhoA signaling pathways that link synaptic strength to sleep pressure, with RhoA activation reducing NREMS delta density while GEF-H1 activation increases it.

papers.title: The DYNAM-O Toolbox: Characterizing Individualized Neural Signatures in Sleep EEG.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Introduces DYNAM-O, an open-source toolbox for detecting transient oscillations in sleep EEG as time-frequency peaks, with feature histograms and dimensionality reduction for individualized signatures. In 112 adults, it replicated higher fast-spindle frequency in females and identified greater low-alpha transient oscillatory activity in females, a novel sex difference ignored by traditional analyses.

papers.title: Juvenile AAV-Mediated MEF2C Gene Replacement Ameliorates Selected Phenotypes in Mef2c-Haploinsufficient Mice
papers.summary: This study tested juvenile AAV-mediated delivery of MEF2C isoforms in Mef2c-haploinsufficient mice, finding improvements in social novelty, sleep, and selected brain measures, indicating modifiable phenotypes during the juvenile period.

papers.title: Assessing accelerometry as an alternative to electromyography for mouse sleep scoring
papers.summary: Assessed agreement between accelerometry and electromyography for manual mouse sleep scoring using hippocampal LFP; overall epoch-by-epoch accuracy exceeded 90% with kappa above 0.8. Accelerometry under-classified Wake by 4.92% and over-classified NREM sleep by 3.29%, indicating slight bias relative to EMG.

papers.title: Modelling shiftwork and sleep fragmentation in mice: behavioural phenotypes and implications for hippocampal neurogenesis
papers.summary: Mice underwent 7 days of either sleep deprivation or sleep fragmentation during their rest phase, and behavioral, neurogenic, and hormonal outcomes were assessed. Sleep deprivation caused progressive reduction in locomotor activity, while fragmentation caused only acute reduction; neither affected hippocampal cell proliferation or plasma corticosterone compared to controls.

papers.title: Repeated morphine reorganizes sleep-wake states, cortical and central medial thalamic oscillations, and network synchronization in mice.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Examined how repeated morphine exposure reorganizes sleep-wake states, cortical and central medial thalamic oscillations, and network synchronization in mice across first and fourth injections and abstinence. Morphine promoted wake, suppressed NREM and eliminated REM sleep; cortex and thalamus dissociated in NREM, with corticocortical alpha synchronization decreased acutely and thalamocortical theta synchronization reduced after repeated exposure.

papers.title: Neuronal ensembles in visual cortex reactivate during hypnagogic sleep onset
papers.summary: Using two-photon imaging of rodent visual cortex, the study found that neuronal ensembles activated by visual stimuli or locomotion show increased reactivation specifically during NREM1 sleep onset after prolonged visual stimulation. Ensembles defined during visual stimulus periods were already present before stimulation, suggesting an endogenous cortical lexicon.

papers.title: Partial sleep deprivation diminishes and uncouples neuronal activity and energy metabolism in the live mouse hippocampus
papers.summary: Using two-photon microscopy in live mice, the study longitudinally tracked spontaneous neuronal activity and tissue partial pressure of oxygen (pO2) in hippocampal CA1 during 7 days of partial sleep deprivation and 7 days of recovery. Partial sleep deprivation progressively reduced spontaneous neuronal activity while sustaining elevated tissue pO2, and after recovery neuronal activity did not return to baseline and oxygenation continued to increase, indicating uncoupling of metabolic and functional recovery.

papers.title: The bidirectional relationship between epilepsy and sleep: a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes the bidirectional relationship between epilepsy and sleep disorders, covering neurobiological mechanisms, clinical implications, and therapeutic consequences. It highlights that NREM sleep promotes epileptiform discharges while REM sleep is protective, and that sleep disturbances lower seizure threshold; targeting sleep disturbances may improve seizure control and quality of life.

papers.title: Xylazine Reshapes the Sleep and Respiratory Consequences of Chronic Fentanyl Exposure in a Sex-Dependent Manner.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Compared chronic fentanyl and xylazine alone and in combination in male and female mice, finding that co-exposure produced sex-dependent sleep architecture changes, exacerbated respiratory depression relative to fentanyl alone particularly in males, and increased peripheral FGF21. Yohimbine partially reversed sleep alterations in a sex-dependent manner.

papers.title: Rapid eye movement sleep deprivation induces a decrease in neuronal nuclear volume in the locus coeruleus, hippocampus and cingulated cortex of the rat.
papers.summary: The study examined the effects of REM sleep deprivation on neuronal nuclear volume in the locus coeruleus, hippocampus, and cingulate cortex of rats. REM sleep deprivation significantly decreased nuclear volume in all three regions, while stress decreased it only in the hippocampus, suggesting changes in metabolic activity.

papers.title: Suppression of corticospinal excitability by sleep spindles without increase in GABAergic inhibition.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using real-time EEG-triggered TMS during sleep, this study found that corticospinal excitability was suppressed during sleep spindles relative to spindle-free NREM sleep, with the lowest excitability during spindle falling phase and trough, but this was not accompanied by modulation of GABA-A receptor-mediated short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI). Slow oscillations increased excitability and reduced SICI irrespective of spindle presence.

papers.title: Sex-associated circadian signaling signatures in the lateral hypothalamus.
papers.summary: Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing, this study compared core clock gene and circadian signaling pathway expression across transcriptionally resolved lateral hypothalamus neuronal populations in female and male mice. It found cell-type-specific sex differences in genes related to intrinsic circadian regulation and sensitivity to VIP, vasopressin, neuromedin, and melatonin receptor signaling despite conserved overall cellular architecture.

papers.title: SleepMambaNet: a lightweight multimodal framework for sleep staging and sleep disorder screening with multicenter validation.
papers.summary: The study developed SleepMambaNet, a lightweight multimodal framework combining efficient channel attention and bidirectional Mamba modules for automated sleep staging and exploratory sleep disorder screening from polysomnographic signals. It achieved high performance across public datasets and a multicenter clinical cohort, with accuracy up to 0.854 and Cohen's kappa up to 0.806, using only 0.47 million trainable parameters.

papers.title: Hyperexcitable but seizure-free: hippocampal network dysfunction in a Wolfram syndrome model
papers.summary: This study characterized hippocampal function in mice carrying a patient-orthologous Wfs1 p.W542* variant and found that dissociated hippocampal neurons were hyperexcitable but showed no increase in network bursting or criticality shift. In vivo, mutant mice exhibited no epileptiform activity or seizures, with male-specific reduced low-gamma power, sex-specific sleep disruption, impaired fear memory, and reduced voluntary motor activity.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea severity associates with reduced phase-lag index functional connectivity during N2 sleep.
papers.summary: In 50 patients with OSA or primary snoring, retrospective polysomnography analysis found that higher apnea-hypopnea index was associated with lower delta-band and theta-band phase-lag index functional connectivity specifically during N2 sleep, while conventional spectral measures showed no significant correlations in any stage.

papers.title: Sleep spindle deficits in childhood absence epilepsy improve with antiseizure treatment and disease resolution.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: In a retrospective analysis of EEGs from 53 children with childhood absence epilepsy (CAE) and 87 controls, sleep spindle rates were reduced in active CAE across cortical regions, most prominently in frontal areas, and normalized after disease resolution. Spindle rate was inversely correlated with epileptic spike rate and varied with antiseizure medication exposure depending on disease state.

papers.title: Blarcamesine improves EEG biomarkers of cortical dysfunction in a mouse model of fragile X syndrome.
papers.summary: This study tested three oral doses of blarcamesine, a sigma-1 receptor agonist, on EEG biomarkers in Fmr1 knockout mice using multielectrode array recordings during resting state and auditory stimulation. Blarcamesine dose-dependently reduced resting-state power including gamma-band elevation and improved inter-trial phase coherence for chirp and 40 Hz ASSR paradigms across cortical regions.

papers.title: REM sleep EEG slowing signals basal forebrain integrity in older adults with subjective and mild cognitive impairment
papers.summary: In 116 older adults with cognitive concerns, greater REM sleep EEG slowing (delta/theta to alpha/sigma/beta power ratio) was associated with smaller nucleus basalis of Meynert volume, and smaller NbM volume was in turn associated with longer sleep latency and poorer episodic memory.

papers.title: Responsiveness of ThymoDream® as a natural modulator of the circadian axis: a comparative RCT with melatonin supplementation employing melatonin profiling and actigraphy.
papers.summary: This randomized, double-blind, active-controlled crossover trial compared ThymoDream (black cumin oil extract, 200 mg) with synthetic melatonin (5 mg/day) over 7 nights in 24 individuals with non-restorative sleep, measuring plasma melatonin under dim light and actigraphy. Both interventions increased nocturnal plasma melatonin, while ThymoDream showed earlier threshold attainment, a more sustained nocturnal melatonin profile, reduced cortisol, and improved daytime sleepiness.

papers.title: Integrating Wearable Temperature, Activity, Melanopic Light, and Lifelog Data to Assess Circadian-Behavioral Coupling in Free-Living Conditions.
papers.summary: This study presents a multimodal wearable and lifelog monitoring workflow combining heat-flux temperature estimation, actigraphy, melanopic light measurement, and web-based lifelog entries to assess circadian-behavioral coupling in ten healthy young adults over one week. The wearable-derived temperature rhythm marker showed a mean absolute difference of 27.1 minutes compared to ingestible capsule gastrointestinal temperature, and exploratory analyses suggested light exposure, activity timing, and behavioral timing provide contextual information for interpreting coupling patterns.

papers.title: Proteoform plasticity modulates the temperature response in circadian timekeeping.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Biophysically characterized an isoform-specific intrinsically disordered region (IDR) of the Neurospora clock repressor FREQUENCY (FRQ) and compared interactomes of two FRQ isoforms, identifying a motif that when altered selectively disrupts timekeeping in a temperature-dependent manner. The findings support a model in which IDRs function as environmental rheostats to enhance clock robustness.

papers.title: Within-cohort discrimination and cross-cohort transfer of EEG-based ADHD classifiers: An exploratory two-cohort evaluation
papers.summary: An exploratory two-cohort reanalysis found that EEG-based ADHD classifiers using Cz/F4, 128 Hz data showed strong within-cohort balanced accuracy in adults (spectral models ~0.95) but not in children (~0.55-0.57), and cross-cohort transfer produced reverse ranking with AUCs mostly below 0.5.

papers.title: Mitochondrial carrier SLC25A34 links clock, diet, and temperature control of adipocyte lipid cycling.
papers.summary: This study identified the orphan mitochondrial carrier SLC25A34 as a convergence point integrating circadian, dietary, and temperature signals in adipocyte lipid cycling. The adipocyte clock represses Slc25a34 via REV-ERB during the sleep phase, while active phase, lipid-rich diet, or cold exposure relieves repression and lipolytic signals induce transcription through PPARs; SLC25A34 is proposed to import oxaloacetate to support the TCA cycle and cytosolic acetyl-CoA production.

papers.title: Differential maturation of mRGC pupillary constriction and circadian rhythmicity in typically developing human infants
papers.summary: Used non-invasive eye-tracking pupillometry and sleep diaries to measure mRGC-mediated pupillary responses to red and blue light in human infants aged 1–12 months. Found prolonged post-natal maturation of mRGC pathways for pupillary constriction that was separate from sleep/wake photoentrainment, with different developmental temporal dynamics.

papers.title: Multimodal PET-MRI profiling predicts dementia with Lewy bodies in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.summary: In 21 patients with isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder, a multimodal covariance pattern of PET and MRI markers (neuroinflammation, cholinergic dysfunction, grey matter atrophy, microcirculatory dysfunction) converged in the medial occipito-parietal cortex; combining this pattern with striatal [18F]-DOPA uptake specifically predicted conversion to dementia with Lewy bodies (sub-distribution hazard ratio = 38.68).

papers.title: Remodeling of the hepatic circadian transcriptome across the estrous cycle.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Explored the circadian transcriptome of mouse liver across the four phases of the estrous cycle, finding that the estrous cycle imposes a ~4-day rhythm on the 24-hour rhythmicity of a considerable proportion of the transcriptome, with largest differences between pre- and post-ovulation phases. Promoter analysis suggests core circadian transcription factors may drive both estrous-cycle and sex-dependent rhythmicity.

papers.title: Light at Night, Night Shift Work, and Cancer: Illustrating Cumulative Exposure to Circadian Disruption through a Thought Experiment.
papers.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
papers.summary: Presents a thought experiment, 'The city that never sleeps,' to illustrate why focusing solely on light at night or night shift work is reductionist, proposing chronodisruption (misalignment between external and internal time) as a link between both pathways and cancer. Outlines six practical steps for designing studies to evaluate cumulative chronodisruption doses, including potential biomarkers.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Modeling of Directed Transfer Entropy Connectivity for EEG-Based ADHD Classification in Children.
papers.summary: The Contextualized Transfer Entropy Network (CTE-Net) was developed to estimate directed EEG connectivity using a Transformer encoder and differentiable transfer entropy for ADHD classification in children. On a public pediatric EEG dataset, CTE-Net achieved 83.4% participant-level accuracy and 90.2% ROC-AUC, while reducing within-subject dispersion of connectivity representations by a median of 38.35% relative to raw EEG.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics reveals cell-type-specific circadian rhythms and their disruption by acute misalignment in mouse aorta.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Single-cell RNA-sequencing of mouse aorta under aligned and acutely misaligned light-dark cycles identified hundreds of cycling genes in vascular smooth muscle cells (SMCs) and fibroblasts, with female SMCs showing higher rhythmicity and more cycling genes than males. Acute misalignment reduced cycling amplitudes and caused limited peak-time adaptation, alongside proteostatic stress signatures in SMCs and in vivo increases in vascular permeability and microvascular thrombus formation in males.

papers.title: Improved Sleep and Clinical Outcomes Following a Single-Session Intervention among Adolescents with Borderline Personality Disorder Features.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: A single-session sleep-focused intervention was tested in 57 adolescents with borderline personality disorder features and sleep difficulties, using ecological momentary assessment and at-home EEG. Post-treatment, multiple objective and subjective sleep indices improved, and several BPD symptom measures also improved significantly.

papers.title: EEG functional connectivity for Parkinson's disease diagnosis and non-motor symptom prediction: a machine learning approach.
papers.summary: Using EEG functional connectivity (debPLI) in 14 Parkinson's disease patients and 14 controls, machine learning with L1-regularized logistic regression achieved 82.14% accuracy in the beta band across four states and 89.29% in the gamma band during eyes-open; theta band connectivity during sadness predicted PSQI scores in patients.

papers.title: The influence of temperature on suicidality in youth: The role of insomnia.
papers.journal: The journal of climate change and health
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 5,590 pediatric psychiatric emergency patients, mean and minimum daily temperatures moderated the temperature-suicidality relationship only in those with insomnia (RR 1.06 per 5°C), and minimum temperature was associated with suicidality through insomnia in a mediation model (OR 1.05).

papers.title: Feasibility and Preliminary Effects of AI-Generated Personalized Sleep Feedback in High School Female Soccer Players: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: This pilot randomized controlled trial evaluated the feasibility of an AI-supported mobile health intervention delivering personalized sleep feedback to 25 high school female soccer players. The intervention group showed a 2% improvement in sleep efficiency compared to controls (95% CI 0.50%-4%; P=.046), with no major technical problems or adverse events.

papers.title: Exploratory EEG Feature Profiles During Viewing of Six Combined Indoor Spatial-Color Conditions.
papers.summary: An exploratory EEG workflow was developed to describe neural feature profiles during viewing of six combined indoor spatial-color conditions in 20 adults, using sequence-aware event mapping and multi-domain feature extraction. The study reports descriptive condition-level values and waveform summaries but no inferential results or pure color/room effects, emphasizing a traceable pipeline for future factorial validation.

papers.title: The trigger-timing framework for long COVID: using symptom triggers and temporal patterns to guide mechanistic stratification and treatment planning.
papers.summary: Proposes a conceptual trigger-timing framework for Long COVID that uses common daily stressors (e.g., upright posture, exertion, meals) and the timing of symptom worsening to infer dominant underlying mechanisms such as autonomic dysfunction, impaired recovery physiology, or mast cell-related processes. The framework is intended to guide mechanistic stratification, diagnostic evaluation, and treatment sequencing but remains hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation.

papers.title: Anti-KLHL11 antibody encephalitis without detectable malignancy: a case report and literature review.
papers.summary: This case report and literature review analyzed 13 cases of anti-KLHL11 antibody encephalitis without detectable malignancy. The most common manifestations were ataxia, dysarthria, and gaze palsy/nystagmus; after immunotherapy, 6 patients improved, 3 remained stable, 4 deteriorated, and 2 died, suggesting that clinical symptoms and neuroimaging cannot reliably distinguish these from tumor-positive cases.

papers.title: Correction: Sleep architecture and lying behavior in horses across age groups and two housing systems: an overnight non-invasive EEG study.
papers.summary: This correction notice addresses an error in a previously published article on sleep architecture and lying behavior in horses across age groups and housing systems using overnight non-invasive EEG.

papers.title: Long-Term Disease Control During Continuous Treatment with Upadacitinib and Baricitinib for Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis: a Real-World Monocentric Retrospective Study.
papers.summary: This monocentric retrospective study evaluated long-term effectiveness and safety of upadacitinib and baricitinib in 41 adults with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. At week 260, 97.1% of upadacitinib-treated patients achieved EASI 75, and all baricitinib-treated patients maintained EASI 75 from week 32 to 312, with infrequent adverse events and no serious adverse events.

papers.title: Cortical Spreading Depression Mimicking Ischemic Stroke: A Case Report of Complex Hemiplegic Migraine with Reversible Cortical Magnetic Resonance Imaging Changes.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 66-year-old man with hemiplegic migraine presenting with acute left-sided hemiparesis and stroke-like MRI findings, including diffusion-weighted hyperintensities without corresponding ADC reduction. The patient improved gradually over 7 days, highlighting the importance of recognizing hemiplegic migraine as a stroke mimic and using MRI ADC status to differentiate from acute ischemic stroke.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
